connections.note: The UAlbany Department of Physics faculty page lists Knuth's appointments as Assistant Professor 2005-2009, Associate Professor 2009-2023, Professor 2023-present, immediately following four years as a GS-14 Research Scientist in the Intelligent Systems Division at NASA Ames (2001-2005). The same page records him as Editor-in-Chief of Entropy (MDPI) since 2012, which is the journal that published the 2019 Nimitz kinematics paper. This is the primary reason the institution is on the board: it is the salaried academic post from which the peer-reviewed UAP kinematics and field-instrumentation literature was produced.

label: Kevin H. Knuth
narrative: Knuth wrote the paper that made the kinematics argument citable. A physicist with a PhD from Minnesota (1995) who spent 2001-2005 at NASA Ames designing AI algorithms for astrophysical data analysis before joining Albany in 2005, he is Editor-in-Chief of the MDPI journal Entropy and works in information physics and Bayesian inference. In September 2019 he published, with Robert Powell of the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies and Peter Reali, 'Estimating Flight Characteristics of Anomalous Unidentified Aerial Vehicles' in Entropy 21(10):939, deriving accelerations, speeds and required power from four documented cases including the 2004 Nimitz encounter. Whatever one thinks of the inputs, the paper did something no amount of testimony could: it put numbers with error bars into a peer-reviewed physics journal, and every subsequent argument about whether the observed performance is achievable with known propulsion has had to engage with it. He is Vice President of UAPx, a research affiliate of the Galileo Project, and co-author of the 2025 UAPx field-expedition paper. The editorship of Entropy is worth noting plainly: a journal editor publishing in his own journal invites the obvious criticism, and the paper's critics have made it.
